item.title: #3614401: Allow install profiles to opt out of being installed
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 27 files, +155/−11 · php +117/−10 · yml +38/−1
  • Diff: 6a4608b
  • Discussion: #3614401 · 3 contributors · 20 comments
  • Followers: 7
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 3 contributors

Summary

Install profiles can now declare that they should never be installed as a module in their own right. Adding opt_out_install: true to a profile's .info.yml tells the installer to skip the step where the profile itself is enabled after its modules and configuration are in place. This is aimed at minimal profiles used for testing or automated environments that have no hooks of their own to run, so there is no reason to keep them installed as a module. Drupal core's own testing and testing_nightwatch profiles are now marked this way.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New opt_out_install key in an install profile's .info.yml lets the profile skip being installed as a module at the end of the installer.

Technical details

The installer reads each profile's parsed info array into $install_state['profile_info'] (via install_profile_info()). install_install_profile() in install.core.inc now checks $install_state['profile_info']['opt_out_install'] before calling \Drupal::service('module_installer')->install() on the profile itself, skipping that call when the key is truthy. drupal_install_system() in install.inc was likewise updated so that the core.extension config's profile key is cleared (not just when there is no profile at all) whenever the profile has opted out, keeping the stored configuration consistent with the fact that the profile was never installed as a module.

Because the core testing profile is used by hundreds of tests and now opts out, several tests that relied on the testing profile's optional configuration (a body field on node, and a locale config override) had to be reworked: the body field was extracted into a new body_field test module, and a new testing_locale profile was added that still gets installed and carries the locale-specific config for the handful of tests that depend on it. A new testing_skip_install profile, whose hook_install() throws an exception, was added purely as test coverage (#3614401's ProfileSkipInstallTest) to prove the opt-out path never runs the profile's install hook. This work builds on #3614153, which moved the System module install step earlier in the installer.

Upgrade

Add opt_out_install: true to an install profile's .info.yml if the profile has no hook_install() or other behavior that depends on being installed as a module:

name: My minimal profile
type: profile
opt_out_install: true

Profiles that rely on optional configuration tied to the profile's own module weight, or that implement install hooks, should not set this key.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: August 1, 2026
  • Committed: August 25, 2026 (24 days later)

Key contributors

  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)
  • nicxvan (nLightened Development LLC)
  • godotislate

Collaboration

nicxvan asked whether there was a clean way to test that the opt-out profile is never installed. catch proposed adding a dedicated test profile whose hook_install() throws an exception, so the test fails if the profile is ever installed; nicxvan agreed and catch implemented it as testing_skip_install with ProfileSkipInstallTest.

item.title: #3610009: Stop discovery of hooks in include files
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +6/−103 · php +6/−98 · yml +0/−5
  • Diff: b1d1929
  • Discussion: #3610009 · 4 contributors · 21 comments
  • Followers: 5
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 4 contributors

Summary

Drupal's hook discovery no longer looks for procedural hook implementations inside include files (.inc) or other custom subdirectories that a module's .module file require_onces. Historically Drupal would scan any file extension and most subdirectories of a module for legacy hook implementations, a leftover from pre-OOP-hooks Drupal. Now only .module, .profile, and .install files (or .theme for themes) at the top level, plus src and src/Hook, are scanned. Modules that still keep procedural hooks in separate include files will find those hooks quietly stop being invoked after upgrading, since discovery simply no longer looks there rather than throwing an error.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: HookCollectorPass (and ThemeHookCollectorPass) no longer scan .inc files, arbitrary subdirectories, or the file_scan_ignore_directories setting for procedural hook implementations; only .module/.profile/.install (or .theme) files and src/src/Hook are scanned.

Technical details

The change is in HookCollectorPass::filterIterator() (and the equivalent in ThemeHookCollectorPass), which decides which files and directories the hook-collecting compiler pass recurses into. Previously, for directories it allowed src/src/Hook unconditionally, and otherwise allowed any directory except tests, js, css (and templates for themes) and any names configured via the file_scan_ignore_directories setting, as long as the directory contained no .info.yml file. For files, it accepted the inc, module, profile, install extensions (inc, theme for themes). This MR strips both mechanisms down: directories are only followed into src or src/Hook, and files are only picked up if their extension is module, profile, or install (theme for themes). inc is dropped entirely and the file_scan_ignore_directories check is removed from this pass (the setting is untouched elsewhere, e.g. ExtensionDiscovery and FileSystem::scanDirectory()).

The motivation, per #3571067, is that hook discovery previously kept scanning include files even though explicit/implicit include-file loading for hooks was removed. Modules that still require_once a separate file with legacy procedural hooks (like better_exposed_filters.module including a helper file) got picked up accidentally, and when they stopped matching (e.g. a leftover include with a stale function name) it produced a confusing InvalidArgumentException: Class "..." does not exist. Removing .inc scanning altogether, instead of trying to special-case or better-report the error, was chosen as the simpler fix since discovery can't reliably tell whether a function in an arbitrary include file is actually a hook. The corresponding kernel tests (testIgnoreDirectories in HookCollectorPassTest and ThemeHookCollectorPassTest) and their fixture test modules/themes were removed along with the code path.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">If a module or theme still implements legacy procedural hooks in a separate include file and loads it manually, for example:

// mymodule.module
require_once __DIR__ . '/mymodule.inc';

// mymodule.inc
function mymodule_entity_type_alter(array &$entity_types) { ... }

move the hook implementation directly into mymodule.module (or mymodule.install/mymodule.profile), or convert it to an OOP hook class under src/Hook. Hooks left in .inc files, or in any directory other than src/src/Hook, will no longer be discovered or invoked, with no error raised.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: July 10, 2026
  • Committed: August 25, 2026 (1 month later)

Key contributors

  • berdir (MD Systems GmbH)
  • nicxvan (nLightened Development LLC)
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)

Collaboration

berdir opened the MR after catch gave a preliminary +1 in Slack to fully removing include-file discovery rather than pursuing the alternative of improving the error message. nicxvan suggested renaming the obsolete test fixture module so the existing test-suite plumbing could still run, which berdir noted was unnecessary because the ignored-directory check itself was being deleted. nicxvan also flagged that gin theme's 5.0.x dynamically glob()s an includes directory from its main theme file, and berdir confirmed that pattern breaks under this change as well, then extended ThemeHookCollectorPass to match. catch committed the change to main, noting it simplifies code that otherwise had to be kept around for years.

item.title: #3577900: Require plugin managers that support annotation discovery to support attribute discovery
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +2/−15 · php +2/−15
  • Diff: 460789d
  • Discussion: #3577900 · 5 contributors · 14 comments
  • Followers: 8
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 5 contributors

Summary

Drupal's plugin system has been moving from PHP annotations to PHP attributes for defining plugins. Since Drupal 11.2, plugin managers that only supported annotation-based discovery (and not the newer attribute-based discovery) triggered a silenced deprecation warning that was easy to miss. As of this change, any plugin manager, in core or in contributed and custom modules, that does not also provide an attribute class will now cause a fatal error when it is instantiated. This is intentional: since many contrib modules define plugin types that other contrib modules provide plugins for, forcing plugin-type-providing modules to add attribute support now (rather than waiting for Drupal 13) gives the wider ecosystem more time to update before the final removal of annotation-only discovery.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Constructing DefaultPluginManager (or a subclass) with only $plugin_definition_annotation_name and no attribute class now throws an \InvalidArgumentException at construction time instead of triggering a silenced E_USER_DEPRECATED notice.

Technical details

The change is in DefaultPluginManager::__construct() in core/lib/Drupal/Core/Plugin/DefaultPluginManager.php. Previously, when a $plugin_definition_attribute_name was passed but did not implement AttributeInterface (i.e. only an annotation class was effectively usable), the constructor called @trigger_error(...) with E_USER_DEPRECATED, which is easy for sites and CI to ignore. Now it throws new \InvalidArgumentException(..., E_USER_WARNING) with a message pointing to the original deprecation change record (drupal.org node 3395582), so instantiating such a plugin manager fails outright rather than warning.

Accompanying core tests were updated: DefaultPluginManagerTest::testDefaultPluginManager() dropped its annotation-only assertions, and testDefaultPluginManagerAnnotationsOnly() now expects the thrown exception message instead of a deprecation message. This does not affect plugin managers that already provide both an attribute class and an annotation class for backward compatibility, which remains the supported pattern; only managers exposing annotation-only discovery are affected. This issue was tracked as a follow-up enforcement of the change documented in the existing change record https://www.drupal.org/node/3522776 (itself a "now you have to do it" successor to https://www.drupal.org/node/3395582 from 2023), so no new change record was created.

Upgrade

If you maintain a plugin manager that extends DefaultPluginManager (or implements similar annotation/attribute discovery) and it currently only supports annotation-based plugin discovery, you must add a PHP attribute class before upgrading to Drupal 12, or code that instantiates your plugin manager will throw:

InvalidArgumentException: Drupal\Your\Namespace\YourPluginManager only supports
annotation-based discovery, which is no longer supported as of Drupal 12.0.
Provide an Attribute class and an Annotation class for BC. See
https://www.drupal.org/node/3395582

To fix, define an Attribute class (implementing the plugin's attribute annotation pattern) and pass both the attribute and annotation class names to the parent constructor, e.g.:

parent::__construct(
  $subdir,
  $namespaces,
  $module_handler,
  $plugin_interface,
  MyPluginAttribute::class,
  MyPluginAnnotation::class
);

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: March 9, 2026
  • Committed: August 25, 2026 (5 months later)

Key contributors

  • berdir (MD Systems GmbH)
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • benjifisher (Harvard Web Publishing)
  • godotislate

Collaboration

Committer catch and berdir discussed how to enforce the requirement: catch initially suggested "unsilencing" the deprecation (making the existing E_USER_DEPRECATED visible) as a middle ground rather than a hard break, and smustgrave agreed, noting modules like entity_embed still lacked attribute support. berdir then implemented the unsilencing approach, but reported in comment #16715227 that he couldn't find a good way to test for an E_USER_DEPRECATED/E_USER_WARNING in this case, and revised the MR to throw an exception instead, explaining "I think I'd prefer that option. We really want contrib to pick this up in D12 IMHO." That became the version that was committed. Separately, benjifisher and catch pushed back on the initial issue title as an unclear double negative, leading to the retitling to its current, clearer form.

item.title: #3303751: Reduce the number of times UpdateRegistry scans for extensions
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +119/−34 · php +118/−33 · yml +1/−1
  • Diff: ee7c7d2
  • Discussion: #3303751 · 5 contributors · 40 comments
  • Followers: 9
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 5 contributors

Summary

Sites with a large number of enabled modules and themes were seeing significantly slower site installs, database updates, and test runs because UpdateRegistry (the service that tracks and runs hook_post_update_NAME() implementations) re-scanned the filesystem for every module, theme, and profile each time it needed to check for update files on a given extension. On a site or test suite with 150+ extensions, this added up to a large, repeated cost. The registry now scans the filesystem for extensions once and reuses the result, cutting a substantial amount of time off installs, updates, and functional test runs, especially on slower filesystems like Docker or WSL2.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: Calling UpdateRegistry::__construct() without the new $memoryCache argument is deprecated in Drupal 11.5.0 and will be required in 12.0.0.

Technical details

The expensive work happened in UpdateRegistry::scanExtensionsAndLoadUpdateFiles(), which built a new ExtensionDiscovery and called scan('module'), scan('theme'), and scan('profile') on every invocation, even though the result rarely changes within a request. This logic was extracted into a new discoverExtensions() method that first checks an injected MemoryCacheInterface (cache.memory) for a cached copy under the update_registry.extensions cache ID, populating it and tagging it config:core.extension on a miss so it's invalidated automatically when the installed extension list changes (module/theme install or uninstall).

To get the memory cache into the class, UpdateRegistry::__construct() gained a new MemoryCacheInterface|string|null $memoryCache = NULL parameter inserted before the existing $updateType parameter. For backward compatibility, if a string is passed in that slot (the old calling convention where $updateType was the sixth argument) it's treated as $updateType and the memory cache falls back to \Drupal::service('cache.memory'), with a deprecation notice raised. The update.post_update_registry service definition in core.services.yml was updated to pass @cache.memory explicitly.

Upgrade

Update any code that instantiates UpdateRegistry directly (for example Drush's deploy hook command) to pass a MemoryCacheInterface service as the sixth constructor argument, before $updateType:

new UpdateRegistry(
  $root,
  $sitePath,
  $module_list,
  $keyValue,
  $theme_handler,
  \Drupal::service('cache.memory'),
  'post_update',
);

Calling the constructor without the $memoryCache argument still works in Drupal 11.5.x but triggers a deprecation notice and will be removed in Drupal 12.0.0.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: August 15, 2022
  • Committed: August 25, 2026 (4 years and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • phma (OM)
  • nicxvan (nLightened Development LLC)
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)
  • longwave (Full Fat Things)

Collaboration

An initial patch from the issue reporter (phma) sat for years before nicxvan and longwave reworked it: longwave proposed an alternative in MR!16818 that avoided threading a boolean flag through several methods and added test coverage proving discovery happens once and is then cached, which nicxvan preferred over the original patch. The two then iterated on whether to use CacheBackendInterface or MemoryCacheInterface (settling on the latter now that #3590964 supported it), and on where the caching logic should live, with nicxvan moving it into discoverExtensions() so any future caller benefits. catch profiled the change against a curtailed run of the node module's GenericTest, confirming it saved about 20 calls to ExtensionDiscovery::scan() (roughly half the time spent in UpdateRegistry::getUpdateFunctions()), and noted the saving multiplies across a full test run executed thousands of times.

item.title: #2871354: Improve "allowed_html" to provide a better config diff
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 30 files, +233/−163 · php +216/−146 · yml +17/−17
  • Diff: 8f7a0cb
  • Discussion: #2871354 · 15 contributors · 126 comments
  • Followers: 23
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 15 contributors

Summary

Text formats that use the "Limit allowed HTML tags" filter store their list of permitted tags/attributes (allowed_html) as a single string. Because elements were historically just appended wherever the admin form or another module happened to place them, two functionally-identical configurations could produce very different-looking strings, making config exports hard to diff and hard to review in version control. Drupal now sorts that list alphabetically whenever it is saved, so equivalent configurations always serialize to the same string and future changes show up as small, readable diffs instead of noise. A one-time update also re-sorts allowed_html on any existing filter format that has Filter HTML enabled, and CKEditor 5's internal list of allowed elements is sorted the same way for consistency.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: The allowed_html setting stored by the Filter HTML (filter_html) plugin is now kept alphabetically sorted; existing filter formats are resorted by a new filter_post_update_sort_allowed_html() update, producing a one-time config diff.

Technical details

The fix lands the simple approach originally proposed in this issue rather than the redesigned, structured schema (nested sequences keyed by element/attribute) that was prototyped and reviewed at length over several years: that redesign hit an unresolved backwards-compatibility problem, since Drupal's config schema has no version tracking, so changing allowed_html from a string to a sequence risked breaking config import from sites still exporting the old string format, a concern raised in the thread by Gábor Hojtsy and effulgentsia.

Instead, FilterHtml::setConfiguration() now runs the incoming allowed_html string through a new public static method, FilterHtml::sortAllowedHtmlTags(), which extracts each <tag attrs> token with a regex and sorts them with sort($tags, SORT_STRING) before re-imploding them. The schema and stored representation remain an unstructured string, so no BC-breaking schema change was needed. A new filter_post_update_sort_allowed_html() (filter.post_update.php) uses ConfigEntityUpdater to resave every filter_format config entity that has an enabled filter_html filter, so the sort applies retroactively without requiring an admin to resave the format manually. Separately, HTMLRestrictions::toCKEditor5ElementsArray() now calls sort($readable) on its own generated element list for the same consistency reason, which is why CKEditor 5 test expectations for allowed-tag strings changed throughout the patch.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: April 20, 2017
  • Committed: August 25, 2026 (9 years and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • sam152 (PreviousNext)
  • dawehner (Chapter Three (acquired by Kanopi Studios))
  • larowlan (PreviousNext)
  • effulgentsia (Acquia)
  • mstrelan (PreviousNext)
  • acbramley (PreviousNext)
  • bbrala (SWIS)
  • borisson_ (Calibrate)
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)
  • wim leers (Acquia)
  • gábor hojtsy (Acquia)
  • dcam
  • quietone (PreviousNext)

Collaboration

This issue was filed in 2017 by Sam152 (sam152) with the simple sorting idea shown in the summary. dawehner offered to help and the conversation quickly escalated into a much more ambitious rewrite: converting allowed_html from a string into a structured, keyed schema (element/attribute maps) to get a genuinely diffable config format, which sam152 iterated on through many patch rerolls, and wim leers gave an unusually thorough line-by-line review (#12092262) praising the "eye to detail" and walking through edge cases like default-configuration merging via FilterPluginCollection::initializePlugin(). That redesign got to RTBC-adjacent state, but larowlan and then Gábor Hojtsy raised a blocking concern: Drupal's config schema has no version tracking, so retyping allowed_html from string to sequence could silently drop or corrupt allowed-HTML settings (a potential security issue) when importing configuration exported by an older core version. Gábor Hojtsy and effulgentsia explored alternatives (a new parallel config key, a union string-or-sequence schema type) but no consensus was reached, and the issue stalled for years on that unresolved BC question before eventually landing with the original, much simpler sorting-only approach.

item.title: #345747: Show all DB Connections on Status Page
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +49/−0 · php +49
  • Diff: 11e9488
  • Discussion: #345747 · 16 contributors · 57 comments
  • Followers: 16
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 16 contributors

Summary

The Status Report page (admin/reports/status) now lists the actual database connection details, host, database name, and table prefix, for every configured database connection, not just the default one. Previously the status page gave no indication of which database(s) a site was actually connected to, which made it easy to mix up databases when cloning or migrating sites for testing. The new "Database connection" (or "Database connections", pluralized when there is more than one) entry surfaces this information directly, including any additional connections such as a replica target.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The fix lives in SystemManager::checkRequirements() in system.module. It calls Database::getAllConnectionInfo() to retrieve every configured connection (keyed by connection name, e.g. default, and then by target, e.g. default, replica), and builds a $requirements['database_connection'] entry with one line per connection/target showing Host: %host (omitted for drivers like SQLite that have no host key), Database: %database, and either Prefix: %prefix or No prefix. The requirement's title uses PluralTranslatableMarkup so it reads "Database connection" or "Database connections" depending on how many are configured.

The accompanying test in SystemTest::testStatusPage() (in core/modules/system/tests/src/Functional/System/SystemTest.php) asserts the presence of the host/database/prefix text, branching on databaseType() === 'sqlite' since SQLite connections have no host key.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: December 11, 2008
  • Committed: August 25, 2026 (17 years and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • arla
  • alexpott
  • daffie
  • nestor.mata
  • tim bozeman
  • cgalli
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)

Collaboration

The issue sat dormant with patches for years before quietone opened a merge request that only reported the default connection's info. Catch flagged in review that "the original feature request was for all database connections" and asked whether the MR should cover that, and daffie agreed. Quietone then reworked the patch to loop over Database::getAllConnectionInfo() for every connection, and in the process caught that $databases['default']['replica'][] = $info_array in settings.php implies an extra level of nesting that also needed handling, updating the code accordingly before daffie set it back to RTBC.

item.title: #3590882: Standard profile should not include Olivero anymore, should provide guidance on how to get started
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 28 files, +471/−209 · php +207/−147 · css +106 · twig +102 · yml +55/−62 · svg +1
  • Diff: 308cba9
  • Discussion: #3590882 · 10 contributors · 66 comments
  • Followers: 13
  • AI disclosures: 1 of 10 contributors

Summary

For new sites installed with the Standard profile, Drupal no longer installs or enables the Olivero theme. Claro becomes both the admin theme and the default front end theme. The site's front page is now a new /admin/welcome page that explains the difference between Drupal Core and Drupal CMS and lists first steps (build a content model, pick a theme, extend Drupal), plus how to change the front page or remove the welcome page by uninstalling the Standard profile. Because that page requires an administration permission, anonymous visitors to the homepage now see a login block instead. None of this affects existing sites: the theme switch and welcome page only apply to fresh Standard profile installs, upgrading a site changes nothing. Installs done via the standard recipe (the CLI/recipe based path) also skip the welcome page and no longer pull in a separate recipe that installed Olivero as the front end theme, since Claro is now set directly.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: Fresh Standard profile installs now set claro as both the admin and default (front end) theme instead of olivero, and set /admin/welcome as the site's front page instead of /user/login.

Technical details

In core/profiles/standard, standard.info.yml no longer lists olivero under themes, and the profile's shipped system.theme config sets default: claro (was olivero). system.site.yml's page.front is now /admin/welcome instead of /user/login. The new standard.welcome route (in standard.routing.yml) is gated by WelcomeController::access(), which checks a standard.show_welcome state flag; standard_install() in standard.install sets that flag only on a fresh install, so already-updated sites never see the page. The old standard_install_finished() status message and its hook_install_tasks_alter() were removed from standard.profile. The page is rendered through a new standard_welcome_page theme hook (Drupal\standard\Hook\StandardHooks) and standard-welcome-page.html.twig, styled by a new welcome-page.css library, and linked from a Welcome admin menu item using a Phosphor signpost icon.

Because the welcome page needs access administration pages, anonymous visitors to the front page now get a 403; a new block.block.claro_login block places a login form in the content region on every page except /user and /user/*, so anonymous users still get a usable homepage instead of a bare error page. Claro gained a user-login-block.css component, and a Classy block--user-login-block.html.twig override renders that block without its default list wrapper. The standard recipe (core/recipes/standard/recipe.yml) drops the now-deleted core_recommended_front_end_theme recipe and sets system.theme.default: claro directly instead of setting page.front and relying on Olivero being installed by that recipe; recipe based installs therefore never see the welcome page and anonymous users still land on /user/login. A number of tests (StandardTestTrait, StandardPerformanceTest, MediaStandardProfileTest, installer and build tests) were updated to reflect the new default markup and page-load query counts now that Claro, not Olivero, renders Standard's front end.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: May 19, 2026
  • Committed: August 25, 2026 (3 months later)

Key contributors

  • gábor hojtsy (Acquia)
  • catch (Third and Grove)
  • lauriii (Acquia)
  • pameeela (Technocrat)
  • xjm (Zoocha)
  • wim leers (Acquia)
  • phenaproxima (Acquia)
  • tim.plunkett (Acquia)
  • pdureau (Beyris)
  • ckrina (Cambrico)
  • quietone (PreviousNext)
  • mherchel (Dripyard)
  • benjifisher (Harvard Web Publishing)
  • rkoller
  • simohell (Druid)
  • the_g_bomb (The University of Edinburgh)

Collaboration

The first version of this change replaced Olivero's welcome content with a one-time status message shown on /user, but a Drupal usability team review rejected that outright: benjifisher reported "strong consensus that a one-time message...is a bad idea" because it disappears on reload, navigation, or a coffee break, and mixes unrelated content like User Guide and event links into a transient message (see #3612901). Following that review, gábor hojtsy rebuilt the feature as a dedicated /admin/welcome page. mherchel and abenbow then raised concerns about the page's verbosity and intended audience, and the group agreed to treat it as an introductory pass to be refined later in the follow-up #3614228 rather than block this issue on design polish. lauriii flagged that the welcome menu's drop icon did not follow Drupal's brand guidelines, prompting gábor hojtsy to swap it for a Phosphor "signpost" icon, and mherchel contributed CSS fixes so the page's two-column layout works correctly in both Claro and the new default_admin theme, including dark mode.

item.title: #3262935: Link field validation constraints don't give enough detail
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 10 files, +64/−50 · php +64/−50
  • Diff: 679a758
  • Discussion: #3262935 · 19 contributors · 69 comments
  • Followers: 20
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 19 contributors

Summary

Link field validation used to show the same generic message, "The path '@uri' is invalid.", for many unrelated problems: an inaccessible path, an unsupported protocol, a URL pointing to a non-existent entity, a missing route parameter, or a URL of the wrong type (internal vs. external) for the field's settings. Editors and developers had no way to tell which of these actually happened without digging into the code. Each failure case now gets its own specific message (e.g. "The URL '@uri' has an invalid protocol.", "The URL '@uri' doesn't exist.", "The URL '@uri' is missing a required parameter.", or a message naming the field when an internal-only or external-only field rejects the wrong kind of link), and messages now say "URL" instead of "path" to match the actual field label used in the UI.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: LinkExternalProtocolsConstraint, LinkNotExistingInternalConstraint, and LinkTypeConstraint no longer have a single $message constructor property; each now exposes multiple named message properties for its distinct failure cases.

Technical details

Following the Symfony validator convention where constraint messages live as properties on the Constraint class rather than being decided ad hoc in the validator, the single $message constructor property on LinkNotExistingInternalConstraint was split into $notFoundMessage, $invalidParameterMessage, and $missingParameterMessage. Summary

Drupal's RouteSubscriberBase class, used to write route event subscribers, previously only supported altering existing routes. It now also supports defining brand new routes, giving module developers an object-oriented alternative to declaring a route_callbacks entry in a *.routing.yml file. As a result, the Views module no longer needs views.routing.yml at all; its route subscriber now builds views routes directly through this new mechanism.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: RouteSubscriberBase::alterRoutes() is no longer abstract; it now has a no-op default implementation, so subclasses that only add routes no longer need to implement it.
  • New API: RouteSubscriberBase::buildRoutes() lets an event subscriber define new routes during the RoutingEvents::STATIC phase, the object-oriented equivalent of a route_callbacks YAML entry.

Technical details

Since routes moved to PHP attribute discovery (#3311365), there was a gap: YamlRouteDiscovery handles the RoutingEvents::STATIC event to add both YAML-defined routes and any route_callbacks, but RouteSubscriberBase only subscribed to RoutingEvents::ALTER. This meant a class that wanted to both define and alter routes had no single, consistent OO entry point for the "define" half.

The fix adds a protected buildRoutes(): RouteCollection method to RouteSubscriberBase, defaulting to an empty RouteCollection, and wires it to RoutingEvents::STATIC via a new onBuildRoutes(RouteBuildEvent $event) listener that merges the returned collection into the event's route collection. alterRoutes() changed from abstract to a no-op default, so a subclass now only needs to override whichever of the two phases it actually uses.

Drupal\views\EventSubscriber\RouteSubscriber was converted to this pattern: its former routes() method (previously invoked via route_callbacks in views.routing.yml) was renamed to buildRoutes() and hooked up through getSubscribedEvents(), and views.routing.yml was deleted since it contained nothing but that route_callbacks entry. The public routes() method is kept, delegating to buildRoutes(), for backwards compatibility; a follow-up issue (#3618565) is postponed to deprecate it once this change is settled.</technical> <parameter name="collaboration">During review, godotislate raised the question of deprecating the now-redundant routes() method on Drupal\views\EventSubscriber\RouteSubscriber, but the decision was to defer that rather than block this change; dcam filed the follow-up, #3618565, postponed on this issue's resolution.

Upgrade

Classes extending RouteSubscriberBase that only need to alter existing routes are unaffected. Classes that previously added new routes via a route_callbacks entry in a *.routing.yml file can instead extend RouteSubscriberBase and override buildRoutes():

protected function buildRoutes(): RouteCollection {
  $collection = new RouteCollection();
  // Add routes to $collection.
  return $collection;
}

No getSubscribedEvents() override is needed for this; the base class now subscribes to RoutingEvents::STATIC automatically.

item.title: #3536795: "Only file JavaScript/CSS assets can be optimized" errors in logs
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +261/−10 · php +253/−10 · yml +8
  • Diff: 72e3f2f
  • Discussion: #3536795 · 11 contributors · 41 comments
  • Followers: 27
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 11 contributors

Summary

Requests for aggregated CSS/JS files that pointed at a stale, invalid, or crafted delta value could crash with an uncaught "Only file JavaScript/CSS assets can be optimized" exception, producing a 500 response and filling logs with errors. This typically happened right after a deployment (which deletes all existing aggregate files) when old cached pages, reverse proxies, or crawlers replayed aggregate URLs whose delta no longer matched a file based group, for example because it now pointed at an externally hosted asset or one marked preprocess: false. Drupal now recognizes this situation and responds with a normal 400 Bad Request instead of throwing an exception, matching how other invalid aggregate requests are already handled.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The delta query parameter is just a position in the list of asset groups that \Drupal\system\Controller\AssetControllerBase::deliver() rebuilds on every request, not a stable identifier. That list also includes groups with type: external or preprocess: false, which are never aggregated and are linked directly in the HTML. When an aggregate file is missing from disk (as happens after drupal_flush_all_caches()) and an incoming delta resolves to one of those non-aggregated groups, deliver() fell through to JsCollectionOptimizerLazy::optimizeGroup() / the CSS equivalent, which threw because JsOptimizer::optimize() and CssOptimizer::optimize() only handle file based, preprocessed groups.

The fix adds a check in deliver() right after resolving $group: if $group['type'] !== 'file' || $group['preprocess'] === FALSE, it throws a BadRequestHttpException('The requested asset group is not aggregated.') before the code reaches the hash comparison and redirect logic (a hash mismatch there would otherwise redirect back to the same non-aggregated group and hit the optimizer again). A new KernelTests\Core\Asset\AssetControllerTest covers this along with the controller's other existing input validation paths, and the functional AssetOptimizationTest was extended to also exercise assertInvalidAggregates() for out-of-range and hash-mismatched deltas after aggregates are deleted from disk. This overlaps with the regression tracked in #3535330 (introduced by #3414173's external minified CSS support) and with the narrower mitigation in #3416508 that skips generating aggregates for stale requests; this fix instead makes deliver() itself reject the request outright.

  • Opened: July 18, 2025
  • Committed: August 23, 2026 (1 year and 2 commits later)

  • herved (European Commission and European Union Institutions, Agencies and Bodies)

Summary

On PostgreSQL, Drupal used to send a separate SET NAMES 'UTF8' statement to the database right after opening every connection, and Drupal opens a new database connection on every request. That statement is now folded into the connection's startup packet instead, so PostgreSQL sites save one network round trip per request. The corresponding $this->connection->exec("SET NAMES 'UTF8'") call was removed from Connection::__construct(); init_commands handling there is unchanged and still runs as before.

Tests added include a kernel test (Drupal\Tests\pgsql\Kernel\pgsql\ConnectionTest) asserting SHOW client_encoding returns UTF8 and that multi-byte UTF-8 strings round-trip correctly, including verifying the DSN setting takes precedence over a PGCLIENTENCODING environment variable. A unit test (Drupal\Tests\pgsql\Unit\ConnectionTest) asserts that constructing a Connection with no init_commands triggers no exec, query, or prepare calls on the underlying PDO object at all, confirming the extra round trip is gone.

Summary

Several core caching methods, CacheableMetadata::merge(), BubbleableMetadata::merge(), and Cache::mergeContexts(), Cache::mergeTags(), Cache::mergeMaxAges(), are immutable-style helpers: they return a new merged result rather than modifying the object they are called on. Forgetting this and discarding the return value is an easy mistake that silently drops cache contexts, tags, or max-age constraints, which can cause incorrect caching and even expose data that should have been varied per user or context. On PHP 8.5 and later, code that calls these methods without using the returned value will now trigger a runtime warning, helping developers catch this class of bug early.

Affects site owners.

  • Requirements: Running on PHP 8.5 or later, code that calls CacheableMetadata::merge(), BubbleableMetadata::merge(), Cache::mergeContexts(), Cache::mergeTags(), or Cache::mergeMaxAges() without using the return value will now emit a runtime warning.

Technical details

The fix adds the PHP #[\NoDiscard] attribute to CacheableMetadata::merge(), BubbleableMetadata::merge() (which calls parent::merge() and further merges attachments), and the three static helpers on Cache: mergeContexts(), mergeTags(), and mergeMaxAges(). #[\NoDiscard] is a native PHP 8.5 attribute; Drupal core's composer.json and Drupal::MINIMUM_PHP already require PHP 8.5.0 on this branch, so the attribute is immediately effective. No method logic changed: merge() still clones $this and returns the merged copy rather than mutating the receiver. This is the same pattern already applied to AccessResult's static constructors and andIf()/orIf() methods and to EntityBase methods in sibling issues, extending the discoverability guard to the cacheability metadata API.

These were carried over from the days when Views was a contributed module and have been removed from core. The issue notes that "Who's online" raises privacy concerns even on community sites, and "Who's new" can expose spam accounts on sites without pre-moderated registration. The views also showed up in the Views UI for every site regardless of whether they were used, and had to be loaded from the database and written to the config cache on every cold cache request, adding a small but non-zero overhead. This is similar in spirit to #3589894, which removed the Node module's Archive, Glossary, and Recent content views for the same reasons.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: The views.view.who_s_new and views.view.who_s_online config entities (and their blocks) are removed from Drupal core; sites that have these views enabled or exported in configuration will need to update their config after upgrading.

Technical details

The change deletes the who_s_new and who_s_online view config entities from core/modules/user/config/install, along with their Spanish translation overrides in core/modules/config_translation/language test fixtures. It also removes the dedicated WhoIsOnlineBlockTest kernel test, since the block it tested no longer exists.

Several other core tests referenced these views incidentally rather than testing them directly, and were updated to use other views instead: ViewUI filter-criteria and tab-CSS tests now use test_content_recent and user_admin_people instead of who_s_online, the views-listing filter test's expected enabled-view count dropped from 4 to 2, and InstallerExistingConfigMultilingualTest's translation-sync assertions were switched from who_s_new/who_s_online to watchdog/archive to keep exercising the same translation-sync logic against views that still exist.

Upgrade

Sites relying on the "Who's new" or "Who's online" blocks or views should recreate equivalent views in Views UI or a custom module before upgrading, since the views.view.who_s_new and views.view.who_s_online config will no longer be provided by the User module:

langcode: en
status: true
dependencies:
  module:
    - user
id: who_s_new
label: 'Who''s new'
...

Any custom code or config export referencing these view IDs (e.g. views_block:who_s_new-block_1 or views_block:who_s_online-who_s_online_block) will need to be updated to point at a replacement view.

item.title: #3582506: Connection::open() should have SensitiveParameter
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +5/−5 · php +5/−5
  • Diff: ac8820e
  • Discussion: #3582506 · 6 contributors · 13 comments
  • Followers: 6
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 6 contributors

Summary

PHP's #[SensitiveParameter] attribute tells the engine to redact an argument's value from stack traces and uncaught exception output. Drupal added this attribute to most sensitive parameters in a previous cleanup (#3296293), but missed the $connection_options argument of Connection::open(), which carries the database password and other connection details. If open() throws an exception or triggers an error, tools that display full stack traces with arguments (such as the Symfony error handler, or PHP configured with zend.exception_ignore_args disabled) could expose the plaintext database password. This fix adds #[\SensitiveParameter] to that argument so it is redacted like other sensitive values.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Database connection credentials could appear in stack traces or error output (e.g. via the Symfony error handler or zend.exception_ignore_args) if Connection::open() throws; the $connection_options argument is now marked #[\SensitiveParameter] so PHP redacts it.

Technical details

The #[\SensitiveParameter] attribute was added to the $connection_options parameter of Connection::open() in the abstract base class (core/lib/Drupal/Core/Database/Connection.php) and in every core database driver's concrete override: mysql, mysqli, pgsql, and sqlite. Since open() is a static method invoked before a Connection object exists, the array containing credentials such as password was previously fully visible in exception backtraces; the attribute causes PHP to substitute an Object(SensitiveParameterValue) placeholder instead when rendering traces.

item.title: #2672340: user_user_role_insert should not exist
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 18 files, +276/−53 · yml +182 · php +94/−53
  • Diff: c9e3af7
  • Discussion: #2672340 · 14 contributors · 70 comments
  • Followers: 17
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 14 contributors

Summary

Previously, whenever a user role was created (through the API, a recipe, or during configuration sync), Drupal silently created two extra configuration entities alongside it: a "user_add_role_action" and a "user_remove_role_action", the actions used for bulk-assigning or removing that role from users. This caused a real bug: an install profile or recipe that already exported both the role and its matching action configuration would fail on install with a ConfigDuplicateUUIDException, because the hook tried to create the action a second time. Now, these helper actions are only created when a role is added through the admin "Add role" UI form. Programmatic role creation (custom code, drush, recipes, config sync) no longer creates them automatically. Maintainers of install profiles or recipes that define custom roles need to also export the corresponding system.action.user_add_role_action.* and system.action.user_remove_role_action.* configuration if they want those bulk actions to exist.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Creating a user_role entity outside of the admin UI role form (via code, drush, config import, or a recipe) no longer automatically creates the paired system.action.user_add_role_action.<rid> and system.action.user_remove_role_action.<rid> config entities.

Technical details

The fix removes the #[Hook('user_role_insert')] implementation (userRoleInsert()) that lived in the user module's hook class and fired on every user_role entity insert, config-synced or not. That logic (skip for the anonymous/authenticated roles, create user_add_role_action.<rid> and user_remove_role_action.<rid> if not already present) is now inlined directly into RoleForm::save(), so it only runs when a role is saved through the admin role-add/edit form. Because the hook no longer runs, standard and demo_umami install profiles and the administrator_role/content_editor_role recipes now ship explicit system.action.user_add_role_action.* and system.action.user_remove_role_action.* YAML config files (e.g. for administrator, author, editor, content_editor roles) instead of relying on the removed hook to generate them at install time. Kernel and functional tests that relied on the old implicit creation (UserActionConfigSchemaTest, BulkFormTest) were updated to create the actions explicitly.

Upgrade

If your install profile, recipe, or custom code creates roles programmatically and you want the bulk "add/remove role" actions to exist, export them explicitly as configuration, following the pattern core now ships, for example:

langcode: en
status: true
dependencies:
  config:
    - user.role.administrator
  module:
    - user
id: user_add_role_action.administrator
label: 'Add the Administrator role to the selected user(s)'
type: user
plugin: user_add_role_action
configuration:
  rid: administrator

Add a matching user_remove_role_action.<rid> file for the remove action. These actions are otherwise only created automatically when a role is created via the admin "Add role" form.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: February 20, 2016
  • Committed: August 17, 2026 (10 years and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • alexpott (Chapter Three (acquired by Kanopi Studios))
  • marcingy (Examiner.com)
  • therealssj
  • larowlan (PreviousNext)
  • joegraduate (The University of Arizona)
  • nicxvan (nLightened Development LLC)
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • quietone (PreviousNext)
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)

Collaboration

The change sat dormant for years after alexpott clarified in comment #18 that user_user_role_insert() "is doing something that does not have to happen at all. It's a UI niceness but from an API point-of-view just gets in the way", distinguishing this from a superficially similar issue (#2980237) raised by idebr. When joegraduate revived the patch, smustgrave pushed back on backward-compatibility grounds, arguing the change could silently break contrib tests and install profiles that rely on the automatic action creation, and suggested a formal deprecation path. joegraduate and nicxvan discussed why a conventional deprecation wasn't practical here since the behavior lives inside a hook implementation rather than an invokable API, with nicxvan noting hook implementations aren't strictly covered under Drupal's BC policy. The resolution that shipped was to update core's own install profiles and recipes to export the actions explicitly, so the fix's own change record documents the migration path for anyone else relying on the old implicit behavior.

item.title: #2934063: Remove the workaround in \Drupal\Core\Installer\ExtensionListTrait::setPathname()
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 15 files, +81/−78 · php +81/−78
  • Diff: 566590d
  • Discussion: #2934063 · 7 contributors · 43 comments
  • Followers: 16
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 7 contributors

Summary

Drupal's installer used to carry a special workaround: a static cache and dedicated InstallerModuleExtensionList/InstallerThemeExtensionList classes that remembered extension file paths across the container rebuilds that happen during installation. That workaround is no longer needed because the base extension list classes can now resolve manually seeded pathnames on their own, so the installer-specific machinery has been removed and the classes that implemented it are deprecated. Along the way, a related bug was fixed: when locating a profile's optional config overrides, ConfigInstaller was looking up the profile's directory using the "module" extension type instead of "profile", which is now corrected.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: Drupal\Core\Installer\ExtensionListTrait, InstallerModuleExtensionList and InstallerThemeExtensionList are deprecated in 11.5.0 with no replacement (base extension list classes now provide the same behavior); use Drupal\Core\Extension\ModuleExtensionList / ThemeExtensionList directly. Drupal\Core\Extension\ExtensionList::setPathname() is also deprecated as an internal-only method with no replacement. All are removed in Drupal 13.0.0.

Technical details

install_begin_request(), InstallStorage::getAllFolders() and ExtensionInstallStorage::getAllFolders() no longer prime ExtensionList::setPathname() for the active install profile; they rely on the base ExtensionList's ability to resolve pathnames added via $addedPathNames directly. NormalInstallerServiceProvider no longer swaps the extension.list.module and extension.list.theme service classes to the installer-specific subclasses. ModuleExtensionList::__construct() now writes container-provided pathnames straight into $this->addedPathNames instead of calling the now-deprecated setPathname().

Drupal\Core\Installer\ExtensionListTrait, InstallerModuleExtensionList, and InstallerThemeExtensionList are reduced to backward-compatibility shims that trigger a deprecation notice on use; they are removed in Drupal 13.0.0 with no replacement, since ModuleExtensionList/ThemeExtensionList now cover the same behavior. ExtensionList::setPathname() itself is also deprecated (it remains @internal) with no replacement.

ConfigInstaller::installOptionalConfig() and getProfileStorages() now call $this->extensionPathResolver->getPath('profile', $profile) instead of getPath('module', $profile) to locate the profile's optional config directory, fixing incorrect path resolution for profiles whose directory structure differs from a same-named module.

Upgrade

Code that extends or type-checks against the deprecated classes should switch to the base extension list classes:

// Before
use Drupal\Core\Installer\InstallerModuleExtensionList;
use Drupal\Core\Installer\InstallerThemeExtensionList;

// After
use Drupal\Core\Extension\ModuleExtensionList;
use Drupal\Core\Extension\ThemeExtensionList;

Any code calling \Drupal\Core\Extension\ExtensionList::setPathname() directly should stop doing so; it is deprecated with no replacement and will be removed in Drupal 13.0.0. All three classes and the method continue to work until then but emit E_USER_DEPRECATED notices.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: January 3, 2018
  • Committed: August 16, 2026 (8 years and 2 commits later)
